opening.text: Most families have a photo on a wall or a shelf. It shows people who belong to each other. Look closely, and you can see the same smile, or the same eyes, passed from one face to the next.
There is a bigger family photo, one we do not see yet. Every person on earth is in it. Today I want to talk about being children of God.

mainMessage.text: We are God’s children. We lived with Him before we were born. We carry something of His nature. We are loved and we have great worth. That truth helps us in hard times, and it changes how we treat each other. It also tells us where we are going: home.

blocks.text: We lived with Him first.
We did not begin at birth. The Lord told Job that when the earth was made, the sons of God shouted for joy. Abraham saw that God knew us before we were born.

Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.

President M. Russell Ballard of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Children of Heavenly Father” at Brigham Young University on March 3, 2020. It is a devotional address, not a conference talk.

There is one important identity we all share now and forever, one that we should never ever lose sight of, and one that we should be grateful for. That is that you are and have always been a son or daughter of God with spiritual roots in eternity. . . . Understanding this truth—really understanding it and embracing it—is life changing. It gives you an extraordinary identity that no one can ever take away from you. But more than that, it should give you an enormous feeling of value and a sense of your infinite worth. Finally, it provides you a divine, noble, and worthy purpose in life.
Our family story goes back before this life.
We carry His image.
The Bible says God made man in His own image. Paul wrote that the Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God, and heirs with Christ.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” read in September 1995 (Ensign, Nov. 1995, 102). It is a proclamation, not a conference talk.
All human beings—male and female—are created in the image of God. Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents, and, as such, each has a divine nature and destiny.
We look like family because we are family.
We are heirs, and we can go home.
John wrote that we are called the sons of God, and that when we see Him, we will be like Him. Heaven’s family is not closed. The way home is open.

Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.

For we saw him, even on the right hand of God, and we heard the voice bearing record that he is the Only Begotten of the Father— That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Missionary Work and the Atonement” in the March 2001 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

The ‘good news’ \[is\] that death and hell \[can\] be escaped, that mistakes and sins \[can\] be overcome, that there \[is\] hope, that there \[is\] help, that the insoluble \[is\] solved, that the enemy \[has\] been conquered. The good news \[is\] that everyone’s tomb \[will\] one day be empty, that everyone’s soul \[can\] again be pure, that every child of God \[can\] again return to the Father who gave them life.
Through the Savior, every child can come home.
Our worth is great.
The Lord told Joseph Smith that the worth of souls is great in His sight. Jesus Christ taught that if God feeds the birds, we are much more to Him.
Remember the worth of souls is great in the sight of God;
Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Face the Future with Faith” from the April 2011 general conference.

Why do we need such resilient faith? Because difficult days are ahead. Rarely in the future will it be easy or popular to be a faithful Latter-day Saint. Each of us will be tested. . . . Persecution can either crush you into silent weakness or motivate you to be more exemplary and courageous in your daily lives. How you deal with life’s trials is part of the development of your faith. Strength comes when you remember that you have a divine nature, an inheritance of infinite worth.
Our worth does not rise and fall with our days.
We are part of His work.
The Lord said His work and glory is to bring to pass our immortality and eternal life. Paul told the people of Athens that in God we live and move and have our being.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring. Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Man Down!” from the April 2009 general conference.

You are enlisted in the Lord’s army in the last dispensation. This is not a time of peace. That has been so since Satan arrayed his forces against our Heavenly Father’s plan in the premortal existence. We don’t know the details of the combat then. But we know one result. Satan and his followers were cast down into the earth. And since the creation of Adam and Eve, the conflict has continued. We have seen it intensify. And the scriptures suggest that the war will become more violent and the spiritual casualties on the Lord’s side will mount.
We have a family mission, and our Father is working with us.
Everyone else is in the photo too.
If we are all God’s children, we are all family. King Benjamin taught that serving others is serving God. And the Savior said what we do for the least of these, we do for Him.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley said this in his talk “The Need for Greater Kindness” from the April 2006 general conference.

No man who makes disparaging remarks concerning those of another race can consider himself a true disciple of Christ. Nor can he consider himself to be in harmony with the teachings of the Church. . . . Let us all recognize that each of us is a son or daughter of our Father in Heaven, who loves all of His children.
If we are His children, we are each other’s family.

story.title: Jesus blesses the children

blocks.text: Parents brought their little children to Jesus Christ. His disciples tried to send them away.

And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them. But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God. Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
The Savior was displeased when the children were pushed away. He took them up in His arms. That is how He sees every one of us.

application.text: First, each morning this week, say to yourself, “I am a child of God.” Mean it. Second, when you see someone who is hard to like, remember that they are God’s child too. Third, tell one person in your life what you value in them.

story.title: God looks on the heart

blocks.text: The prophet Samuel was sent to anoint a new king. He looked at a tall, strong young man and thought, surely this is the one.

But the Lord said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
We judge by what we can see. God looks at the heart. That is good news for us. It means that He sees who we truly are, and He still calls us His children.

application.text: First, write down three things you are grateful you inherited from your Father in Heaven. They might be gifts, talents, or ways you love others. Second, notice when you judge by appearance, and try to see the heart. Third, thank God for making you His child.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they felt their worth as a child of God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The father runs to his son

blocks.text: A young man had wasted his inheritance. He decided to go home and ask to be a servant. His father saw him far off.

And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
The son said he was no longer worthy. The father did not agree. He still called him my son. A child of God may feel unworthy, but God has not stopped seeing a son or a daughter.

application.text: First, think of a time you felt you did not belong. Remember that you are expected in God’s family. Second, write a note to someone to remind them of their worth. Third, kneel in prayer and call Him “Father” with your whole heart.

The First Presidency and the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” read in September 1995 (Ensign, Nov. 1995, 102). It is a proclamation, not a conference talk.
All human beings—male and female—are created in the image of God. Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents, and, as such, each has a divine nature and destiny.
We have a divine nature and a divine destiny.
Heirs of the family.
John wrote that we are God’s children now, and when He appears we will be like Him. Through the Savior, the family can be together again.

Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.

For we saw him, even on the right hand of God, and we heard the voice bearing record that he is the Only Begotten of the Father— That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Missionary Work and the Atonement” in the March 2001 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

The ‘good news’ \[is\] that death and hell \[can\] be escaped, that mistakes and sins \[can\] be overcome, that there \[is\] hope, that there \[is\] help, that the insoluble \[is\] solved, that the enemy \[has\] been conquered. The good news \[is\] that everyone’s tomb \[will\] one day be empty, that everyone’s soul \[can\] again be pure, that every child of God \[can\] again return to the Father who gave them life.
We do not inherit alone. We inherit together.
Our value is on the record.
The Lord said the worth of souls is great. Jesus Christ taught that God cares for the birds, and we are worth much more.
Remember the worth of souls is great in the sight of God;
Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Face the Future with Faith” from the April 2011 general conference.

Why do we need such resilient faith? Because difficult days are ahead. Rarely in the future will it be easy or popular to be a faithful Latter-day Saint. Each of us will be tested. . . . Persecution can either crush you into silent weakness or motivate you to be more exemplary and courageous in your daily lives. How you deal with life’s trials is part of the development of your faith. Strength comes when you remember that you have a divine nature, an inheritance of infinite worth.
What we are worth is written in heaven.
What the family is doing.
Our Father is at work. The Lord said His work and glory is to bring to pass our immortality and eternal life. Paul said that in God we live, move, and have our being.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring. Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Man Down!” from the April 2009 general conference.

You are enlisted in the Lord’s army in the last dispensation. This is not a time of peace. That has been so since Satan arrayed his forces against our Heavenly Father’s plan in the premortal existence. We don’t know the details of the combat then. But we know one result. Satan and his followers were cast down into the earth. And since the creation of Adam and Eve, the conflict has continued. We have seen it intensify. And the scriptures suggest that the war will become more violent and the spiritual casualties on the Lord’s side will mount.
We each have a part in the family work.
All on the same record.
If we are God’s children, so is everyone else. King Benjamin said that serving our fellow beings is serving God. The Savior said that what we do to the least of these, we do to Him.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley said this in his talk “The Need for Greater Kindness” from the April 2006 general conference.

No man who makes disparaging remarks concerning those of another race can consider himself a true disciple of Christ. Nor can he consider himself to be in harmony with the teachings of the Church. . . . Let us all recognize that each of us is a son or daughter of our Father in Heaven, who loves all of His children.
Every person we meet is a sibling in His family.

story.title: My Father and your Father

blocks.text: Mary Magdalene stood outside the tomb. She did not know that the man in front of her was Jesus Christ. Then He spoke her name.

Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.
He knew her by name. And He called His Father her Father. The Savior has always included us in the family. He did not say, my Father. He said, my Father and your Father.

application.text: First, write down what you know to be true about who you are. Keep it where you can read it. Second, speak to one person this week the way you would speak to a sibling in a family you love. Third, pray to your Father in Heaven by name. Tell Him what is on your mind.

There is a bigger reunion ahead of us. Today I want to talk about being children of God.

mainMessage.text: We belong to God’s family. We lived with Him before this life. We carry His image, and we are heirs of what He has. Our worth is great and does not change. That helps us in trials, gives us purpose, and calls us to treat every person as family.

blocks.text: We were family before we met.
God asked Job where he was when the earth was laid, when the sons of God shouted for joy. Abraham learned that we were known and chosen before birth.

Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.

It gives you an extraordinary identity that no one can ever take away from you. But more than that, it should give you an enormous feeling of value and a sense of your infinite worth. Finally, it provides you a divine, noble, and worthy purpose in life.
We have known this family before.
You have His laugh.
We resemble our Father. The Bible says He made us in His image. Paul wrote that the Spirit witnesses to our own spirit that we are children of God and heirs with Christ.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. story.title: Our Father which art in heaven

blocks.text: The disciples asked Jesus Christ how to pray. He started with one short phrase.
After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
He taught them to begin with “Our Father.” He could have chosen any title. He chose the one that says we belong to Him, and to each other. Every prayer is a family conversation.

application.text: First, start your next prayer with “Our Father.” Say it slowly and mean it. Second, greet one person you do not know well, as you would a relative. Third, thank God for something that makes you feel part of His family.
